chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Five supplications are not blocked from the Lord, Blessed and Exalted: The supplication of the equitable Imam; and the supplication of the oppressed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic says: "I shall exact revenge for you, even if it be after a while"; and the supplication of the righteous child for his parents; and the supplication of the righteous father for his child; and the supplication of the believer for his brother in his absence, so He says: "And for you is the like of it".'

key_terms.بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ: In his absence / behind his back
key_terms.لَأَنْتَقِمَنَّ لَكَ: I shall exact revenge for you

ai.seo_question: What are the five supplications that are never blocked from God?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights five supplications that are guaranteed acceptance, emphasizing the spiritual authority of the equitable Imam and the reciprocal nature of intercessory prayer among believers. Notably, the promise of divine vengeance for the oppressed is explicitly linked to the Imam's supplication, reflecting the Shia concept of divine justice (Adl) and the efficacy of du'a in both personal and communal spheres. The inclusion of parents and children underscores the familial dimension of spiritual merit, while the believer's prayer for another in their absence illustrates the interconnectedness of the Ummah.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Myasws fatherasws was saying: ‘Five supplications would not be Blocked from the Lordazwj Blessed and High – A supplication of the equitable Imamasws; and a supplication of an oppressed, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “Iazwj shall Exact Revenge for you and even though it may be after a while”; and a supplicatin of the child for its parents, and a supplication of the righteous father for his children, and a supplication of the Momin for his brother in his absence, so Heazwj would be Saying: “And for you is the like of it”’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

My father (a.s.) has said, ‘Five kinds of prayers are not barred from the Lord, the Most Blessed, the Most High: the prayer of an Imam who is just in his dealings, the prayer of an oppressed as Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, “I will revenge for you even if it may come after a long time,” the prayer of a virtuous son for his parents, the prayer of a virtuous father for his son and the prayer of a believing person for his brother (in belief) in his absence to whom it is said, ‘You will have as your reward just like what you asked for him.’”
